findings.title: Mist and atmosphere are much thinner and less dynamic than the reference
findings.evidence: Reference at the rest framing (Loop camera static; S210 and S320 register to S000 within 0.1 px) vs the lane, pinned clear and misty at t30. (a) No veil climbs the massif: misty minus clear on its lower-mid face (180-360 x 300-390) is -13 (L090) and -17..-19 (S320-S330) in the reference vs -4 in the lane. (b) The bank stays see-through over the plain: base (0-360 x 390-450) hp std is 0.97-1.13 in the reference vs 1.80 in the lane, with the same mean (161-164 vs 163). (c) The right side is static: the reference's mist at the iceberg's foot comes and goes (berg_face 110->116->105->113 over the Loop, an/loop_berg_shadow.jpg); the lane's bank box ends at x = -6 m. (d) In the reference the massif dims well above any bank and partly recovers (upper-left 184->167 at L120, 172-175 at S300-330; upper-right 179->168->181), while the engine's terrain light never changes. Forensics: the sun is at (-0.828, 0.321, -0.459), 18.7 deg up, about 2/3 of the light on sun-facing snow. The 6 cards were drifting, alpha-opaque cards in the Cycles render. bake_env_m9.py makes the cards camera-invisible only, so the bake keeps their shadows frozen at the .blend positions. Side by side: an/mist_1to1_L090.jpg, an/mist_1to1_S210_S320.jpg, an/massif_veil_2x.jpg, an/loop_massif_shadow.jpg, an/loop_signed_diff.jpg, an/hold_bases_vs_ref.jpg (the reference's hold fog sea is also billowier).
findings.fix_hint: Measure first, then extend ATMOS_MIST, each part behind its own switch. 1) Add an upper, thinner steel-blue veil over the massif's foot, up to about 15-25 m, sized so misty minus clear on 180-360 x 300-390 reaches -13..-17. 2) Make the low bank denser so the plain's hp falls to about 1.0 at full bank while the base mean stays 161-164; the left columns at the ridge foot are already at or above the reference, so keep them. 3) Add a bank lobe at the iceberg's foot (around x +20..+45, z -60..-80) on the Loop's timing (3x). 4) Before building cloud shadows, render the v7 scene in Blender with the cards shadow-visible at two drift offsets. If that reproduces the reference's massif dimming, take the moving cards' alpha along the sun ray to dim the env's sun share (world-anchored, carried by uCloudShift), and drop the frozen card shadows from the bake.

findings.title: Low cloud cards now sweep a veil across the far range
findings.evidence: an/far_range_veil_1to1.jpg and an/right_side_over_time.jpg: at t90 and t150 the far range left of the iceberg is washed out. F000 shows it unveiled, with grey-blue shading. Card 4 (cloud_b, 139.8 m deep, bottom at y -3.6 m) and the other low cards draw in front of the range, which is painted on BG001 at 359 m (builder's open item 4). far_range_R is 196.5 vs 184.6 in F000. findings.fix_hint: Make the far range occlude the low cards as it does in F000. Take the range's crest profile from BG001's painted silhouette (rest-camera tangent u -> v) and fade or discard card fragments below the crest in CLOUD_FRAG, using the same orbit-aware projection the cards already use. Alternatively, have the ENV bake give the range an alpha or depth occluder on BG001. Re-check far_range_R at t3.4, t90 and t150.

summary:
I judged the atmos lane from fresh captures of my own lab on :5176 (since stopped), compared with MAIN :5173 and every reference frame; everything is in WORK/judge1 and verdict_draft.md. The verdict is FAIL with a lens score of 7.6.

**The user's main complaint is fixed.** Clouds no longer disappear when the page is left alone. I checked 144 frames from 3.4 s to 24 h at 9 pointer positions, a 95 s live run, and T0, T2, phone and ultrawide; every frame has natural clouds. They drift left as one smooth, rigid loop with an exact 404.76 s period, and no cloud ever jumps on screen. The clouds sit where F000 has them at the first rest frame, and the summit puff is the left cloud's edge, as in the reference.

**What passes:**
- The iceberg and dark ridge colours are closer to F000 than before.
- The hold background is closer to F402 / F420 than the integrated build, and the fake static puff is gone from the hold.
- Press, hold and release have no pops.
- `?atmos=r10` restores the integrated build exactly (≤0.41/255 vs MAIN with the rings masked).
- Cost is about +3% (paired timing; the method's own noise is ±8%).
- No errors, typecheck 0/0, and the 3-way merge onto MAIN has no conflicts.

**What fails:**
- **Major:** the mist the user asked for is much thinner and less alive than the reference's.
  - The reference fog bank veils the massif's lower face (−13 to −19 levels when misty); the lane manages −4.
  - The reference bank hides the plain; the lane's lets the plain show through.
  - Mist at the iceberg's foot comes and goes in the reference; the lane's right side never changes.
  - In the reference the massif darkens well above any fog and partly recovers, probably from the moving clouds' shadows. The engine's terrain light never changes, and its bake keeps the clouds' shadows frozen where the original file had them. This needs a quick Blender render to confirm before anyone builds cloud shadows.
- **Minor:** low clouds now drift in front of the distant mountain range and wash it out as they pass (t90, t150), which F000 never shows.

**Nits:** the drift speed is at the low end of the reference's range. Panel scoring against F000 must pin the time to 3.4 s, or the sky will be misread. The white summit and flat dark ridge belong to the environment bake, not this lane.
